newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Bonn coalition tight-lipped on '98 budget talks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bonn coalition tight-lipped on '98 budget talks.

text.p: Leaders of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition government on Wednesday slapped a news blackout on the state of negotiations on Germany's 1998 budget after fresh talks failed apparently to achieve a breakthrough.

Although Hermann Otto Solms, chief budget negotiator for junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP), said the talks were "good and promising", no details emerged from a morning meeting at Kohl's federal chancellery.

Coalition sources said a budget deal could only be achieved next week at the earliest, since Kohl and other top government officials will fly to the group of seven summit being hosted by the U.S. in Denver this weekend.

One man staying behind is Finance Minister Theo Waigel, who newspaper reports said will have his work cut out to close a huge 32 billion mark ($18.5 billion) gap in the 1998 budget. Waigel has pledged to meet the fiscal criteria governing European monetary union while accepting FDP demands not to raise taxes.
Newspapers said on Wednesday that progress was being made in horse-trading on the budget, with Waigel looking to dock around five billion marks from departmental budgets next year.
